correctness.rationale: Full direct proof: convex complements in a tree are single-edge sides; all supports of size <=2 are shattered; a triple is shattered exactly when it has no point between the other two; compatible tree splits forbid a four-point shattering. Unique middle-point counting gives W(T)-binom(n,2) unshattered triples. Edge-cut distance formula yields sharp star/path cases. Standalone checker independently reconstructed graph geodesic convexity for all 1,442 labeled trees up to six vertices and 120 deterministic larger cases.

value.rationale: The theorem determines the full natural shattering-support distribution for every finite tree, not merely a VC dimension or finite benchmark. Its exact cubic coefficient recovers the classic Wiener metric index and transfers sharp extremal path/star behavior to a learning-theoretic invariant. Characterizing all shattered supports and providing an interpretable relation between traces and aggregate distances is a substantive structural bridge, independent of any downstream conjecture.
